Hi, please make sure to fill out the full form as provided, this includes each of the following sections:

```
### Tested versions

### System information

### Issue description

### Steps to reproduce

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)
```

MRP is important because it also determines if the problem is specific to your project or applies broadly to the engine, and gives us something common to test against to establish if the issue is fixed.

>

>

>

> ```

> MRP is important because it also determines if the problem is specific to your project or applies broadly to the engine, and gives us something common to test against to establish if the issue is fixed.

To avoid misunderstanding - I will say it directly. This is an engine problem. If it were a project problem, I would have written that it is a project problem or related to it. Besides, why do you think I didn’t check this before writing? If I omitted empty items, it is because they don’t matter. My job is to report the problem, not to investigate it; that is your task. I provided the information as fully and accurately as possible, as I have done before. I hope you understand my position.

Engine problems can also be caused by specific inputs/values or sets of inputs/values, which makes it useful to have an MRP to compare against. We also have no way of knowing when something is omitted from an issue whether it was omitted on purpose or by accident, whether that was because it was misunderstood or it was forgotten - hence why we ask people to fill out the entire template and why people often write 'N/A' if they feel it is truly not applicable.

It's also worth bearing in mind that Godot is an open source project primarily supported by volunteers, it isn't my job to investigate any specific problem, I donate some of my time to help triage issues and investigate problems or fix them when I am able to, much like many others. It is a collaborative effort of research, testing and fixing that makes these projects work while remaining free and open. Myself and many others are more than happy to investigate many of these issues in our spare time, but it helps us to do so when we are provided all the information we might need in a consistent manner, and that also involves people who report the issues working with us. Generally people are much less likely to pick up and work on issues with incomplete or unclear information, which is part of why we ask for it when doing triage if it isn't already present, since it can help your problem get resolved faster too.

That's exactly what I'm saying - this is your job. There's nothing wrong with people simply wanting to work on their projects, encountering bugs, and just reporting the issue. Personally, I rarely have the time to dig into these things, but I try to provide as much information as I can for others. If it were just about personal benefit, like you mentioned, I wouldn’t even be writing this here.

You're right that we can't always know the exact cause, but based on my experience and what I observed, this looks like a micro bug related to a boolean - something I've often seen in the UI here. So if you're working on this, then yes, you're voluntarily contributing to it. I'd be glad to help and so on, but I'm just reporting obvious bugs so others are aware and can fix them. I'm not concerned with how quickly it's resolved.

The first thing that should’ve been done was to check whether this issue appears in the same engine version in a blank project. That's why there's no MRP - it was marked as "empty" and later removed for clarity. You can check that too. So again, I hope you understand this position - it's impossible to do everything at once, but a person can still point out specific issues.

I can confirm this on 4.5.beta 7c472e655.

We should make it so the `(x changed)` text always appears consistently. If the user enables the feature at runtime using a script, then the changed properties *will* have an effect, so it's important that the user is able to spot this.

In version v4.5.stable.official [876b29033], v4.6.dev1.official [8d8041bd4] this still occurs.
